failure_reason: At step 13 the agent’s replacement for GUIProcess._on_error constructs the non-Windows hint as "(Hint: Make sure '<command>' exists and is executable.)" with an extra period before the closing parenthesis. The test expects the message to end exactly with "(Hint: Make sure '<command>' exists and is executable)" (no trailing dot). This punctuation mismatch propagates into the final implementation, causing msg.text.endswith(...) to fail.

Step 18 introduced normalizeHomeDirPathForWindows but it reads os.Getenv("USERPROFILE") instead of the required "userprofile" env var. In the tests, only "userprofile" is set (lowercase), and on non-Windows systems env vars are case-sensitive, so USERPROFILE is empty and the helper returns the original path (~/.ssh/known_hosts). This directly causes TestNormalizedForWindows to fail.

Step 19 is the earliest deviation: the agent implemented ReadAtMost to return nil when it reads exactly `limit` bytes and the subsequent probe read returns io.EOF. However, the repository’s tests define the contract that hitting the limit boundary (including limit==len(content)) must return ErrLimitReached because the function cannot know whether more data exists without reading past the limit. The implementation’s post-read probe (`n, err := r.Read(1)`) returns EOF for strings.NewReader("hello") after consuming 5 bytes, so it incorrectly returns nil instead of ErrLimitReached, directly causing the observed test failure.

In step 1, the agent’s plan/mental model diverged from the requirements: it decided that BraveAdBlocker.read_cache should catch deserialization errors, show a message, and then *raise* a new DeserializationError. However, the PR requirements and the failing test expect read_cache to handle corrupted cache data internally (emit an error-level user message) and then continue without propagating any exception. This incorrect intent directly caused the later code change (raising DeserializationError from read_cache), which made test_corrupt_cache_handling fail because the exception escaped the method.

Step 10 is the first point where the agent commits to the wrong Register semantics: it replaces Register’s logic with a version that *only* calls PlayerRepository.FindMatch(userName, client, userAgent) and, on any error, creates a new Player with uuid.NewString(). This drops the existing required behavior (seen in step 6) where Register first checks the provided id via ds.Player(ctx).Get(id) and returns that same player when found. As a result, when tests call Register(ctx, "123", ...), the code no longer loads player ID=123 and instead creates a new UUID, causing p.ID != "123" and failing the tests.

In step 22, makeRequest was modified to return a generic HTTP status error on JSON unmarshal failure with non-200 status, but the error string was formatted as fmt.Errorf("last.fm http status: %d", resp.StatusCode), producing "last.fm http status: 500". The updated test expects the exact string "last.fm http status: (500)" (with parentheses). This mismatch in formatting directly causes the failing spec for non-200 HTTP responses with non-JSON bodies.

Step 30 is the earliest causal deviation: it modified BraveAdBlocker.read_cache to convert adblock deserialization failures into a new DeserializationError and re-raise it (lines 232/237). The requirements/tests expect read_cache itself to catch deserialization errors, emit message.error("Reading adblock filter data failed... Please run :adblock-update."), and return without propagating any exception. By raising DeserializationError from read_cache, the exception escapes (as shown in the failure stack trace), so the test fails before it can assert the user-facing error message.

Step 24 is the earliest causal deviation: the agent attempted to modify scanner/serverapi.go to stop returning errKernelVersionHeader for Debian when X-Vuls-Kernel-Version is missing, but the str_replace_editor action clearly failed (its observation shows repeated directory listings instead of an edit result). Because the edit didn’t apply, ViaHTTP still contains `if family == constant.Debian && kernelVersion == "" { return ..., errKernelVersionHeader }`, so TestViaHTTP continues to error on the Debian-without-kernel-version case. Later steps (26/27) further show the editing session became corrupted, but the root cause for the failing test is that the required code change was never actually committed starting at step 24.

In step 4, the agent modified ScanResult.isDisplayUpdatableNum() but placed the FreeBSD override after the `if mode.IsFast()` block that returns `true` for the default case. For `mode=Fast` and `Family=FreeBSD`, execution enters the fast-mode branch and hits the `default: return true` before reaching the later `if r.Family == config.FreeBSD { return false }`. This directly causes the test failure `[10] expected false, actual true`. The FreeBSD check must be evaluated before any fast-mode returns (or included in the fast-mode switch) so it always forces false regardless of scan mode.

Step 8 changed find_match to only try find_quick_match then find_threshold_match, removing the existing find_exact_match fallback. This over-tightened/altered matching so records without identifiers but with strong exact metadata (title+author+publisher+publish_date) no longer match existing editions, leading to creating a new edition instead of modifying the existing one. That directly causes test_covers_are_added_to_edition to see reply['edition']['status']=='created' rather than 'modified'.

Step 5 rewrote Display.display to lock using self._lock.acquire()/finally: self._lock.release() instead of `with self._lock:`. The unit test replaces `_lock` with a MagicMock and asserts `lock.__enter__` was called, which only occurs when the lock is used as a context manager. Since acquire/release never calls __enter__, the test sees 0 calls and fails; the method then writes directly to stdout, matching the captured output.

The agent attempted to update models/vulninfos.go Cvss3Scores via a Python string-replace, but the action did not actually modify the file (the observation shows unrelated directory listings and later step 34 confirms the original code remained). Because Cvss3Scores stayed unchanged, it passed the full pipe-joined severity string (e.g., 'not yet assigned|low') into severityToCvssScoreRoughly, which cannot map that composite label and returns 0. This directly caused the failing test expecting score 3.9 while preserving 'NOT YET ASSIGNED|LOW'.

The earliest deviation is step 20, where the agent first implemented InPlaylist/NotInPlaylist in operators.go with an incorrect SQL string. It used `SELECT pl.media_file_id` (qualified with alias) and `WHERE playlist.id = ?` instead of the required subquery `SELECT media_file_id FROM playlist_tracks pl LEFT JOIN playlist on pl.playlist_id = playlist.id WHERE (pl.playlist_id = ? AND playlist.public = ?)` (note unqualified `media_file_id`, join `on` casing, parentheses, and filtering by `pl.playlist_id`). This wrong literal directly caused the ToSql output mismatch in the failing tests for inPlaylist/notInPlaylist.

Step 3 is the earliest deviation: after grep output already showed the failing tests call Bookshelves.update_work_id, the agent committed to a single-path plan focused only on Booknotes and concluded the deletion-on-conflict logic in CommonExtras.update_work_ids_individually was 'opposite of what's required'. It then proceeded to reproduce/fix behavior for Booknotes by removing the delete-on-conflict path in CommonExtras. But CommonExtras is shared by Bookshelves/Booknotes/Ratings/Observations; Bookshelves.update_work_id relies on the existing behavior to resolve collisions by deleting the old (conflicting) row so the old work_id disappears. By changing the shared logic to never delete on conflict, the old bookshelves_books row with work_id=1 remains, causing the test assertion 'old work_id 1 present' to fail.

Step 9 is the earliest causal deviation: the agent attempted to patch authenticate via a brittle str_replace of a small error-handling block, but it did not add the required guard/early-return when FindByUsernameWithPassword returns ErrNotFound (usr remains nil). As a result, authenticate still proceeds to call validateCredentials(usr, ...) with usr==nil for invalid users / token auth, causing the nil pointer dereference seen in tests instead of returning Subsonic error code 40 and stopping the handler.

The earliest causal deviation is in step 22 where custom_headers was rewritten to gate Accept-Language with `if accept_language is not None:` (and similarly for the per-domain branch). In qutebrowser config, missing values can be represented by the `usertypes.Unset` sentinel, which is not `None`. When the test calls `custom_headers(url=QUrl(...), fallback_accept_language=False)` with no per-domain override, `config.instance.get_obj(..., fallback=False)` returns `Unset`, the `is not None` check passes, and the code executes `accept_language.encode('ascii')`, raising `AttributeError: 'Unset' object has no attribute 'encode'`. The correct check must treat `Unset` like “not set” (e.g., compare against `usertypes.UNSET`/`usertypes.Unset` or use config APIs that return `None`), so Accept-Language is omitted as required.

The agent unconditionally added a new 'languages' key to AmazonAPI.serialize() output (line 334) even when no language data exists, resulting in 'languages': [] being present for responses without languages. The failing test compares the entire dict exactly and expects no 'languages' key for the fake API response (content_info is ''), so the extra key causes AssertionError. The fix should conditionally include 'languages' only when extracted languages are present (non-empty) or when the API provides a languages field, matching existing output shape expected by tests.

In load_book.py import_author, the new remote_ids merge is wrapped in `try: ... except Exception: pass`, which swallows AuthorRemoteIdConflictError raised by Author.merge_remote_ids when incoming remote_ids conflict with the matched author’s existing remote_ids. In the failing test, find_entity matches by OL key (/authors/OL4A) whose viaf=87654321, then merge_remote_ids would detect conflict with incoming viaf=12345678, but the broad except prevents the error from propagating, so pytest sees no exception. The fix is to not catch AuthorRemoteIdConflictError (or re-raise it) and only ignore non-conflict errors if needed.

Step 72 introduced the first incorrect implementation of _AnsibleUnicode for bytes inputs: it decodes bytes using UTF-8 when encoding is not provided (result = str(object, encoding='utf-8', ...)). The requirement and failing test expect legacy types to match base str() semantics: _AnsibleUnicode(b'Hello') should behave like str(b'Hello') -> "b'Hello'" (no decoding) unless encoding/errors are explicitly passed. This mismatch directly leads to the observed failure where result was 'Hello' instead of "b'Hello'". Later steps (99/146) retained the same default-decoding behavior, but step 72 is the earliest point where the causal bug was committed.

Step 23 introduced the command-concatenation logic that unconditionally re-adds the address-family context when rt_commands is non-empty: `if rt_commands: if not commands or commands[-1] != 'address-family %s unicast' ...: commands.append('address-family ...')`. In the failing test, `route_target_both_auto_evpn=True` already caused `commands` to include `address-family ipv4 unicast` followed by `route-target both auto evpn`. Because the last command is not the AF header, this new block appends a second `address-family ipv4 unicast` before adding manual route-target commands, producing `... 'route-target both auto evpn', 'address-family ipv4 unicast', 'route-target import ...', ...` instead of the expected sequence without the duplicate AF line. If this step had been implemented to avoid re-entering AF when already in AF context (or to structure commands so AF header appears only once), the test would pass.

At step 19 the agent committed to an incorrect dictionary schema for Standard Ebooks entries, changing map_data to read entry['language'] and entry['dc_issued'] (and previously publisher). The real dictionary-based feed used by tests provides language under 'dcterms_language' and publish timestamp under 'published' (publisher under 'dcterms_publisher'). Because of this mismatch, map_data raises KeyError('language') when called with SAMPLE_1, causing the test failure. The fix should instead read entry['dcterms_language'] (validate startswith 'en-') and derive publish_date from entry['published'][0:4], while publishers remains ['Standard Ebooks'].

At step 3 the agent committed to the wrong consolidation strategy: it decided to introduce a single map[models.CveContentType]models.CveContent ("merge CveContent of the same type") to merge all entries per source/type into one. This violates the requirement that additional entries for the same source are allowed when they represent distinct CVSS records with different Cvss2Score/Vector or Cvss3Score/Vector. By collapsing everything into one per source, later code overwrote CVSS fields (keeping only one record) and removed expected additional records, producing the test diffs where [1] entries were removed and remaining [0] entries had different CVSS values. The correct approach is to deduplicate only identical CVSS tuples and separately join multiple severities (e.g., LOW|MEDIUM) without collapsing distinct CVSS records.

Step 28 introduced truncateCell with incorrect truncation semantics: it truncates via content[:MaxCellLength] and then appends FootnoteLabel immediately (e.g. "th[*]") without adding an ellipsis ("...") and separating space, and without reserving space for the suffix within MaxCellLength. The updated AddRow then computes column widths from these shorter strings, producing narrower header/separator widths. The tests expect truncated cells to render as "<prefix>... <FootnoteLabel>" (e.g. "Trains are much better th... [*]") and for widths to reflect that rendered value. This misinterpretation in step 28 is the earliest causal deviation leading to the TestTruncatedTable output mismatch.

The controller implementation of Chats.messages.edit returns the updated message nested under `response.message` (`helpers.formatApiResponse(200, res, { message: messages[0] })`). The v3 API tests expect the updated message object to be returned directly as `response`, so `body.response.content` exists. With the current code, the content is at `body.response.message.content`, making `body.response.content` undefined and causing the assertion failure. The earliest point this incorrect response shape was introduced is step 31.

Step 10 introduced a nil-pointer dereference by setting `PURL: vuln.PkgIdentifier.PURL.String()` in `contrib/trivy/pkg/converter.go` (line 106). In Trivy results, `PkgIdentifier` and/or `PkgIdentifier.PURL` can be nil (as in the test JSON fixtures), so calling `.String()` on a nil `*packageurl.PackageURL` panics with SIGSEGV during `Convert`, causing `TestParse` to fail. The correct implementation must safely handle missing PURL (e.g., `if vuln.PkgIdentifier.PURL != nil { purl = vuln.PkgIdentifier.PURL.String() }` else empty string), and similarly for `p.Identifier.PURL`.

The earliest deviation is in step 28 when the agent created scripts/providers/isbndb.py and implemented is_nonbook as: binding_lower = binding.lower(); for nonbook in nonbooks: if nonbook.lower() in binding_lower: return True. This only matches when the NONBOOK phrase is contained within the binding string. The test expects is_nonbook('cassette', NONBOOK) == True because 'cassette' should match the NONBOOK entry 'Audio Cassette' via token/word matching (i.e., binding token contained in a NONBOOK phrase, or symmetric substring matching). With the implemented direction, 'audio cassette' is not a substring of 'cassette', so it returns False, causing the failing test case.

Step 24 is the earliest causal deviation: the agent attempted to update redis/sorted.js via a single str_replace using an exact old_str match and injected heavily escaped quote sequences. In this repo the target function text didn’t match that exact old_str, so the replacement likely did not apply (or produced malformed literals like '\"\"\'-inf\"\"\''), leaving sortedSetsCardSum effectively unchanged and still summing full zcard values. As a result, calls with (keys,'-inf',2) ignored the bounds and returned 7 instead of the filtered 5, causing the test failure.

In step 9, the agent rewrote TocEntry.to_markdown() and introduced an extra leading space when level==0 and label is missing. The new logic builds `result = '*' * self.level` (empty for level 0), then unconditionally appends a space in the no-label branch (`result += ' '`), and then appends the delimiter string starting with a space (`result += f" | {title} | {pagenum}"`). For level 0 this yields `'  | Chapter 1 | 1'` (two leading spaces) instead of the required `' | Chapter 1 | 1'` (one leading space), causing the failing test. The correct implementation must ensure exactly one leading space before the first `|` when level=0 and no label is present (e.g., by not adding an extra space when there are no stars/label, or by constructing the prefix as `('*' * level) + (' ' + label if label else '')` and then adding the delimiter with a single leading space).

Step 5 inserted `import "io"` as a separate import statement after the existing parenthesized import block in log/formatters.go (line 8 in the snippet). Go forbids having an `import` declaration in the middle of a file after another import block; this makes the package fail to compile, so the test suite cannot run. The correct change would have been to add `io` inside the existing import (...) block (or merge imports), not create a second import section.

The agent changed scanner/walk_dir_tree.go:dirStats to add field ImageFiles []string instead of the required/tested field name Images (slice of image filenames). The scanner tests assert collected[baseDir].Images contains cover.jpg; since the struct no longer has Images, Gomega reports 'missing expected field Images' and the suite fails. Fix: keep/add dirStats.Images []string (and populate it in loadDir) while optionally mapping to album ImageFiles later.

In step 7 (Requirement Analysis), the agent commits to an incorrect R128→ReplayGain normalization formula: it states and then builds tests around `ReplayGain_dB = (R128_Q7.8/256) - 5.0` (a -5 dB offset). This is the earliest point where the mental model diverges from the repository’s expected loudness reference. The failing specs show the correct normalization should effectively be `+5.0` relative to the agent’s implementation: input `"0"` must yield `5.0` but the implemented formula yields `-5.0`, and `"-3776"` must yield `-9.75` but the implemented formula yields `-19.75` (exactly 10 dB too low). This wrong assumption propagates into the later code change (getR128GainValue subtracting 5), directly causing the test failures.

Step 24 is the earliest deviation: when implementing Posts.uploads.deleteFromDisk in src/posts/uploads.js, the agent added input validation that throws new Error('[[error:invalid-data]]') for non-string/non-array inputs. The updated tests expect a specific error key/message: '[[error:wrong-parameter-type, filePaths, object, array]]' when an object is passed. Because the function always throws the generic invalid-data error, the assertion fails. Fix: change the thrown error to the expected wrong-parameter-type format (including parameter name and actual/expected types) when typeof filePaths is neither 'string' nor Array.isArray(filePaths).

Step 17 is the earliest causal deviation: the agent restructured routes() to make getOpenSubsonicExtensions public but still wrapped it with the checkRequiredParameters middleware. The new test calls /getOpenSubsonicExtensions?f=json with no v/c/u/p; checkRequiredParameters rejects missing required params and returns an error response that unmarshals but leaves Subsonic.OpenSubsonicExtensions nil. The spec then dereferences *response.Subsonic.OpenSubsonicExtensions and panics. The endpoint must be registered outside BOTH authentication and required-parameter validation (or required-parameter rules must exempt this endpoint), so it can succeed with only f=json as in the test.

Step 8 is the earliest deviation: the agent attempted to patch /app/src/socket.io/posts/votes.js to add the required topics:read privilege enforcement, admin bypass, UID deduplication, and cutoff response. However, the observation shows the command did not apply the edit at all (it printed repeated repository directory listings instead of a successful replacement diff/confirmation). As a result, SocketPosts.getUpvoters remained in its original insecure form and continued returning upvoter data even when guests lacked topics:read, causing the test to fail with 'Missing expected rejection' for [[error:no-privileges]].

The ffmpeg parser’s parseInfo/extractMetadata logic stores the raw channel descriptor (e.g., "stereo") into tags["channels"] (step 25 lines 162-166). The PR/tests require converting descriptors like mono/stereo/5.1 into the corresponding channel count and storing that numeric value in the metadata map (tests expect []string{"2"}). Because ffmpeg_test asserts directly on extractMetadata output (not via Tags.Channels()), returning "stereo" causes the 4 failing specs. The fix should convert match[1] to an integer count (e.g., via a small mapping or shared helper) and store it as a numeric string in tags["channels"].

Step 34 introduced logic that strips a trailing '
' from the final combined decoded output (`if combined.endswith('
'): combined = combined[:-2]`). This misinterprets the requirement 'should not append any extra newline at the very end': the function must not add *additional* newlines beyond what decoding produces, but it must preserve control characters that come from decoding `_x000D_`/`_x000A_` tokens. In the failing test, the last `<S>` element decodes to `' 
'`, so trimming removes that legitimate final CRLF, yielding output ending with `b' '` instead of `b' 
'`, causing the assertion failure.

Step 27 is the first causal deviation: it modifies construct_rule() to append the multiport match early (lines 548-551) before append_param(rule, params['jump'], '-j', False). This causes generated iptables commands to place '-m multiport' before '-j ACCEPT'. The unit test TestIptables.test_destination_ports asserts the opposite ordering ('-j', 'ACCEPT' must precede '-m', 'multiport', '--dports ...'), so this early insertion directly leads to the observed argument-order mismatch and test failure.

Step 51 is the earliest deviation: the agent attempted to update public/src/modules/helpers.common.js spawnPrivilegeStates to add a data-type attribute, but the action did not actually modify the file (the observation is just a directory listing, and later Step 65 confirms the function still renders <td data-privilege=... data-value=...> with no data-type). Because the helper remained unchanged, helpers.spawnPrivilegeStates returned HTML missing data-type, causing the assertion failure in test/template-helpers.js.

Step 24 rewrote utils/lastfm/client.go makeRequest to return the generic error string "unexpected status code: %d" when HTTP status != 200 (including the branch where JSON unmarshal fails). The tests expect the legacy generic message format "last.fm http status: (500)" for non-200 responses with non-JSON bodies. Because this step introduced the wrong error text (and removed the previous behavior), the client.ArtistGetInfo call returns an errorString with "unexpected status code: 500", causing MatchError("last.fm http status: (500)") to fail.

The agent only modified selectTranscodingOptions to special-case reqFormat=="raw" and suffix-match-without-bitrate, but did not change determineFormatAndBitRate’s precedence rules for player MaxBitRate vs transcoding DefaultBitRate. In the repository, determineFormatAndBitRate applies MaxBitRate only when p.MaxBitRate < trc.DefaultBitRate; with DefaultBitRate=96 and MaxBitRate=192 it leaves bitrate at 96. The failing test expects MaxBitRate to be used as the default when no explicit bitrate is requested, regardless of being higher than the transcoding default. Because step 12 omitted updating this logic (e.g., choosing MaxBitRate whenever present and reqBitRate==0), selectTranscodingOptions returns ("oga",96) instead of ("oga",192), causing the test failure.

Step 36 introduced the faulty caching logic in getCACert: it always looks for a per-instance cache file named "<server name>-ca.pem" and only writes that file for CloudSQL. But RDS/Redshift downloads are cached under the URL basename (e.g. rds-ca-2019-root.pem) via ensureCACertFile. Therefore after rds.SetCA(nil), initCACert calls getCACert, which fails to find "rds-ca.pem" and triggers downloader.Download again, making fakeDownloader.count go from 1 to 2 and failing TestInitCACertCaching. The fix is to have getCACert check/read the correct cached filename per DB type (RDS/Redshift: URL-basename file; CloudSQL: instance-name file) before downloading.

Step 38 is the earliest deviation: it introduced _replace_stderr_clixml with logic that drops a CLIXML block when _parse_clixml returns empty bytes (commented as 'Empty result, just skip the CLIXML block entirely'). In the failing test, stderr is exactly a CLIXML block containing only <Objs Version="foo">\r\n</Objs> (no <S S="Error"> entries), so _parse_clixml returns b'' and the function returns b'' instead of preserving the original bytes unchanged. This directly causes assert b'' == original to fail.

The earliest causal deviation is in step 25 where CRLFWriter was implemented to only wrap/convert when runtime.GOOS == "windows" and otherwise return the original writer unchanged. The new tests expect CRLFWriter to perform LF→CRLF normalization in the test environment (linux CI), so returning the raw buffer leaves "
" unchanged, producing the observed failures ("hello
world..." instead of "hello
world..."). This also breaks the cross-write case because the wrapper isn’t applied at all, so the second write’s leading "
" is not converted. If CRLFWriter had been implemented without the GOOS gate (or with a testable/forced Windows mode), the tests would pass.

Step 6 introduced the incorrect no-label formatting in TocEntry.to_markdown: it set label_seg to a single space when label is missing, but the f-string already inserts a space after the stars (f"{'*'*level} {label_seg} | ..."). For level=0 this produces two leading spaces before the first pipe (and for higher levels even more), violating the required output (exactly one leading space when no label). This misinterpretation caused the test_to_markdown failure observed at step 7.

The agent prematurely committed to fixing the issue by changing QuerySet._clone() to copy _known_related_objects, assuming shared dict state caused deferred-field leakage. This was a wrong mental model for the reported nested-prefetch overwrite bug (parent instance from outer queryset overwriting inner-prefetched parent with different deferred fields). Additionally, the validation command failed because pytest wasn’t available, so the agent never verified behavior. As a result, the real prefetch caching logic remained unchanged and the nested prefetch still triggered an extra SELECT, causing the test failure.

The earliest causal deviation is in step 25 when rewriting qutebrowser/config/configutils.py: Values.__str__ was changed to format patterned entries as "<opt.name>['<pattern_str>'] = <value_str>" (see the new lines.append("{}['{}'] = {}"...)). However the repository’s tests (and existing expected behavior) require the legacy format "<pattern_str>: <opt.name> = <value_str>" (e.g. "*://www.example.com/: example.option = example value"). This incorrect requirement interpretation directly produced the failing output shown in test_str, causing the assertion mismatch.

Step 25 is the first causal deviation: the converter change did not correctly implement the PR requirements. It still stores binary package Version as p.Version without combining with p.Release, so versions remain truncated (e.g., libgnutls30 3.6.7 instead of 3.6.7-1+deb10u1). It also attempts to set Arch from p.Arch, but the parsed Trivy package struct used by this repo does not populate that field (or uses a different field name), so Arch stays empty in output. Finally, source package creation logic was not reliably changed from the original `if p.Name != p.SrcName` gating; as a result, when binary and source names are identical (adduser, apt), no SrcPackage entry is created, matching the test diff showing those SrcPackages removed. These omissions directly lead to the failing TestParse diffs for missing SrcPackages, empty Arch, and truncated versions.

Step 34 introduced the core bug: in get_location_and_publisher, when parsing colon segments it does `locations.extend(_remove_brackets(l) for l in all_locs)` without dropping entries that become empty after bracket removal. For loc_pub='[Place of publication not identified] : Pearson', the phrase removal leaves '[] : Pearson'; get_colon_only_loc_pub returns loc='[]', and _remove_brackets turns this into '' which is then appended, producing ([''], ['Pearson']) instead of ([], ['Pearson']). Filtering out empty strings after removing brackets (or removing the unidentified-place phrase including brackets) would prevent the failing test.

The earliest causal deviation is at step 11, where luqum_replace_child was changed to always copy the old child’s formatting whitespace (head/tail) onto the replacement node. In the failing test, the old child `id:2` appears as the right operand of `OR` inside a group and carries a leading space in its `head` (rendering as `OR id:2`). The replacement expression is itself a Group-like node that, per expected output, must render immediately after the operator with no intervening space: `OR(subject:horror)`. By copying `head=' '` from `id:2` onto the replacement, the function forces `OR (subject:horror)`, introducing the extra space seen in the failure. The correct behavior is to rebuild children without blindly inheriting head/tail (or to apply different whitespace rules depending on node type), so this unconditional whitespace preservation is the direct ancestor of the formatting mismatch.

Step 20 is the earliest deviation: it explicitly checks out (reverts) sphinx/writers/latex.py (removing the earlier % insertion in the generated LaTeX source) and applies a macro-level fix in sphinxlatexstyletext.sty (\sphinxcode uses \unskip...\ignorespaces). This cannot satisfy the requirement/tests that inspect python.tex and expect literal '%' comment markers immediately after \sphinxupquote{ and before the closing braces (\sphinxupquote{%\n...%\n}}). By abandoning the writer-level change, the produced .tex lacks those '%' markers, leading to the assertion failure.

The repository had valid code changes (confirmed by git diff --stat at step 150), but the agent never executed the required final submission command (`echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && git add -A && git diff --cached`). Instead, starting at step 148 it continued creating/running extra scripts and only viewed `git diff` (unstaged). Because nothing was staged and no cached diff was produced, the harness reported 'No patch generated by agent'. The earliest deviation is step 148 where the agent should have transitioned to the mandated submission step after tests passed (step 147) but did not.

Step 35 introduced/retained an unconditional "Don't upscale the image" early-return in resizeImage: `if originalSize <= size { return nil, originalSize, nil }`. With square=true, tests expect the output to be exactly `size x size` and encoded as PNG regardless of source, even when the original image is smaller (e.g., 100px) than the requested size (200px). Because of this guard, resizeImage returns nil (no resized image), so resizedArtworkReader falls back to returning the original bytes, yielding 100px dimensions and jpeg format for jpg inputs. The fix is to bypass the no-upscale early-return when square==true (and likely always produce a square canvas of the requested size, upscaling the fitted image as needed) so square requests always return size x size PNG.

Step 24 introduced the new prepare_multipart() implementation in lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py, but its multipart serialization does not match the required/fixture format used by the tests. In particular it emits headers in a different order (it writes Content-Disposition before Content-Type for file parts, while the fixture expects Content-Type first), it omits a Content-Type header for plain text fields (fixture includes Content-Type: text/plain / application/octet-stream for form_field_*), and it does not apply the expected base64 encoding + Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64 for on-disk file reads (file4–file6 in the fixture). These byte-level formatting differences are exactly what the failing assertion reports (diff at index 70 shows Content-Type vs Content-Disposition), so this is the earliest causal deviation leading to test_prepare_multipart failure.
